_note: Labelled cases for the VERDICT surface. Measured by services/api/verdict-eval.ts, which is deliberately separate from ask-eval.ts: Ask is 'what does this document say', verdict is 'what follows from the evidence in front of the panel'. One accuracy number over both would hide which of the two failed.
_groundTruth: EVERY label follows from the ruleset applied to the findings, not from a toxicology opinion. R1 states human-cell evidence defeats animal in vivo evidence for human hepatotoxicity, so a case whose only live human evidence asserts toxicity has one supported answer. A case with no consequence-half evidence at all cannot support a severity call, whatever the mechanism half says - that is true by construction, and it is the category a confident system gets wrong. Each case names the reason under `why` so a reader can disagree with the label rather than take it on trust.
_provenance: Findings follow the shape of data/probe-case.json, which was generated from this project's own evidence streams. Compound labels are real drugs from the library so the prose reads as it would in use; the FINDINGS are constructed to isolate one decision each, and no case claims to reproduce that drug's actual regulatory outcome.

rules.name: Human relevance
rules.statement: Human-cell evidence defeats animal in vivo evidence when the question is human hepatotoxicity.

rules.name: Exposure relevance
rules.statement: A finding at an exposure far above the projected human Cmax carries less weight than one at or near it.

rules.name: Reversibility
rules.statement: Damage that reverses on withdrawal is weaker evidence of a safety concern than damage that persists.

cases.why: Live human-cell evidence asserts toxicity at clinical exposure and nothing contests it. R1 makes human evidence decisive for this question, so there is one answer the evidence supports.

_presentField: `present` is the inventory: which checklist items the panel actually has, tagged by half. A first version of this fixture omitted it and every case came back cannot_conclude - correctly, because adjudicator-v1.2 requires a severity verdict to NAME consequence-half evidence, so a package declaring none has no basis to commit on. The model was right and the fixture was wrong. It is set explicitly on every case now, and the cannot_conclude cases are the ones whose consequence half is genuinely empty.
